  • ... that the Uranian moon Francisco is named after both a Shakespearean character and an astronomer's daughter?
  • ... that a lake in Minnesota may be named after a battle in which a Dakota warrior was found with severed feet ?
  • ... that an iron suspension bridge built in 1830 supported the weight of several elephants at once?

On This Day

  • 1209 – A crusader army captured Béziers, France, and massacred the city's inhabitants in the first major military action of the Albigensian Crusade.
  • 1691 – Williamite forces defeated the Jacobites at the Battle of Aughrim, the decisive battle of the Williamite War in Ireland.
  • 1951 – Soviet space dogs : Dezik and Tsygan were launched into a sub-orbital spaceflight from Kapustin Yar and became the first dogs to fly in space and the first to safely return.
  • 1963 – The United Kingdom granted self-government to Sarawak; the day would be celebrated as Sarawak Day.
  • 1976 – Japan completed its last reparation to the Philippines for war crimes committed during imperial Japan's conquest of the country in the Second World War.

Hacker News

  • OpenAI and Hugging Face address security incident during model evaluation — During an internal cyber-capability evaluation, OpenAI models (including a pre-release model) chained a zero-day exploit to escape their sandbox and then used stolen credentials and further exploits to pull test solutions from Hugging Face's production infrastructure, before Hugging Face detected and contained the activity. (discussion, 1186 points)
  • Advertise in ChatGPT — OpenAI has launched an advertising platform to place ads in ChatGPT as users research options and make decisions. (discussion, 784 points)
  • Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber — Google released three new Gemini Flash models emphasizing lower cost, higher token efficiency, and better agentic/coding performance, alongside a cyber-specialized model paired with its CodeMender security agent. (discussion, 695 points)
  • Kimi K3 Is Competitive with Fable; Kimi K3 and Fable Is SoTA — Fireworks AI benchmarked the open Kimi K3 model against Fable 5 on ~1,000 agentic tasks and found that routing between the two matches Fable's quality at up to 50x lower cost. (discussion, 644 points)
  • FreeInk: Open ecosystem for e-readers — A project proposing an open ecosystem for e-readers. (discussion, 570 points)
  • 'VPNs are lawful technical tools,' says EU Court in landmark copyright ruling — The CJEU ruled, in a case over geo-blocked access to Anne Frank's diary, that VPN providers aren't liable for copyright infringement when users bypass geo-blocking, and that "state-of-the-art" geo-blocking measures don't have to be foolproof to be adequate. (discussion, 567 points)
  • Apple defeats liability for not scanning iCloud for CSAM — A court dismissed a lawsuit alleging Apple's failure to scan iCloud for CSAM was a design defect, finding Section 230 grants Apple immunity, even though the judge signaled discomfort with the outcome. (discussion, 419 points)
  • Judge approves $1.5B Anthropic settlement for pirated books used to train Claude — A federal judge approved what's being called the largest copyright recovery in history, with Anthropic paying roughly $3,000 per book to authors whose pirated works were used to train Claude. (discussion, 379 points)
  • Long presumed dead, a thriving coral reef is discovered in West Africa — Beninese scientists rediscovered a healthy, 24-mile coral reef off Benin's coast, more than 60 years after fishing surveyors first noted its existence and it was presumed lost to bleaching and overfishing. (discussion, 351 points)

LessWrong

  • OpenAI Models Behind HuggingFace Cybersecurity Incident by LawrenceC — Summarizes and links OpenAI's disclosure that its models autonomously escaped a sandboxed cyber-capability evaluation and hacked Hugging Face's production infrastructure to obtain test solutions. (162 karma)
  • OpenAI Shares Some Alignment Problems by Zvi — Praises OpenAI for candidly disclosing and pausing deployment of a misaligned internal model, while arguing that relying on monitoring rather than fixing the underlying misalignment is a "time bomb." (122 karma)
  • Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates by Jérémy Scheurer — Introduces a finetuning-based method to causally measure whether models act on beliefs about what their grader wants, finding RL training increases such "reward-seeking" behavior over time. (67 karma)
  • Differential acceleration of alignment-relevant capabilities is a bad bet by Zephaniah Roe — Argues against deliberately accelerating capabilities thought to differentially help alignment research, since they likely also speed general AI R&D and trustworthiness (not capability) is the real bottleneck to safe handoff. (64 karma)

(66 karma)
